title: Gas composition and methane loss at nine Danish commercial biogas upgrading plants
article_citation: Kvist, T.; Aryal, N. (2019). Methane loss from commercially operating biogas upgrading plants. Waste Management, 87, 295–300.
transcription_source: IEA Bioenergy Task 37 (2025), Reduction of methane emissions from biogas systems and landfills, Table 6, pp. 13–14; that report attributes the nine-plant table to Kvist and Aryal (2019). The separate RTO result is transcribed from the original article abstract.
license: Reuse license not identified for the original Waste Management article or the IEA Bioenergy report in the accessed records. Source identities and short factual observations are retained for internal traceability; redistribution rights require review.
source_location: IEA Bioenergy Task 37 report Table 6, pp. 13–14; original article abstract for the RTO result
derivation: Transcribed the nine plant rows shown in the IEA report's Table 6 and one abstract-level RTO methane-removal result. No gas compositions were normalized or recalculated. Empty cells mean the IEA table did not list that constituent; explicit zeros remain numeric zero.
study_scope: Gas was sampled at three amine, four water-scrubber, and two membrane upgrading facilities at commercial Danish biogas plants. The primary article abstract reports an overall mean methane loss of 0.81% relative to methane supplied to the upgrading units and a 99.5% methane-emission reduction in a regenerative thermal oxidizer follow-up test.

column_basis.feed_gas_*_pct: Before-upgrading gas composition percentages as reproduced in the IEA report. The report labels these gas quality percentages but does not explicitly state a molar or volume basis in the table.
column_basis.product_gas_*_pct: After-upgrading biomethane composition percentages as reproduced in the IEA report. No conversion or renormalization was applied.
column_basis.offgas_*_pct: Upgrader waste-gas composition percentages as reproduced in the IEA report. No conversion or renormalization was applied.
column_basis.methane_loss_pct: Percent of methane supplied to the upgrading unit, per the primary article abstract.
column_basis.rto_ch4_removal_pct: Reported percentage reduction of methane in upgrading waste gas after a selected regenerative thermal oxidizer test; the abstract does not provide the plant ID or detailed test conditions.

applicability: Phase 6 reference for technology-specific gas composition and methane losses; can inform measurement planning and technology comparison only. It is not a GreenHub raw-gas specification or default.
limitations: Plant identities, feedstocks, plant scale, upgrader throughput, pressure, time averaging, and replicate uncertainty are not provided in the reproduced table.
Gas percentages are retained as reported and may not sum to 100% because of rounding, omitted constituents, or incomplete reporting; no balance closure or normalization is implied.

The IEA table does not explicitly define the gas-composition percentage basis as volume or mole fraction. The published methane-loss denominator is separately identified as methane supplied to the upgrader.
Missing composition cells remain blank and are not interpreted as zero. Explicit source-reported zeros remain zero.
The RTO result is a separate follow-up on selected waste gas and is not paired to an identified plant row in the IEA table.

These are Danish commercial biogas installations, not measurements on GreenHub grass-derived gas, and the plant-level values must not be treated as a representative probability distribution or a single plant default.
No open reuse license was identified for either source; redistribution rights should be reviewed before external publication.
